message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to two different mammalian orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade that contains both of those orders, which is a placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago. It was likely a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived in the early Paleocene, before the diversification of the modern groups of carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
